name: Cuneiform & the clay tablets of Sumer
strand: Languages & scripts born in a place
scope: The mud-brick cities of Sumer in southern Iraq (Uruk), plus Nineveh's great library and Darius's cliff at Behistun. T1: in Sumer the world's OLDEST writing was pressed into wet CLAY with a cut reed -- the wedge marks we call cuneiform ('cuneus' = wedge in Latin). T2: it was invented not for poetry but for BOOKKEEPING -- the first tablets at Uruk are receipts counting sheep, grain and beer. T2: the reed stylus makes triangular WEDGES because you cannot drag a curve through wet clay, so the early pictures collapsed into abstract wedge-clusters. T3: because it is baked/dried CLAY, when a city burned the tablets fired hard and SURVIVED -- fire destroys paper but preserves clay, which is why hundreds of thousands remain. T3: cuneiform was never one language -- for ~3,000 years it was reused to write Sumerian, then Akkadian, Babylonian, Hittite (a shared writing 'operating system'). T3: Mesopotamian numbers were BASE-60 (sexagesimal) -- the reason a circle has 360 degrees and an hour 60 minutes traces to Sumer. T4: the Epic of Gilgamesh, the oldest great story, survives on twelve clay tablets from Nineveh's Library of Ashurbanipal (7th c. BCE), and Tablet XI tells a FLOOD story older than Noah. T4 (dinner-test): in 1872 George Smith, reading a Nineveh tablet in the British Museum, found that Flood story and reportedly grew so excited he began tearing off his clothes -- the first modern person to read a lost 2,600-year-old tale. T5: how cuneiform was CRACKED -- on a cliff at Behistun in Iran, Darius the Great carved the same boast in three cuneiform languages, and Henry Rawlinson copied it dangling on ropes, using it as cuneiform's 'Rosetta Stone'. T5: one wedge-sign could be a whole word, a syllable, OR a silent 'determiner' tag that labels a category -- one sign doing three jobs, which is why it resisted reading for so long.

framing_note: Scene-led, place always in the stem (Sumer/Uruk/Nineveh/Behistun); invert the wonder -- lead with the huge number/mystery, make the knowable fact the answer (300,000 surviving tablets -> 'because fire BAKES clay'). Key accuracy rail: cuneiform is a SCRIPT reused across many languages, not a language -- keep stems saying 'cuneiform', not 'the Sumerian language'. Dinner-test payoff: George Smith and the Flood tablet. Behistun is the decipherment rung (pairs with the Rosetta Stone ladder as the two great trilingual keys). Lane border: the PLOT of Gilgamesh and Mesopotamian empire history belong to history/mythology -- here every answer is about the WRITING and its PLACE (the tablet, the library, the cliff), never the epic's storyline.
history_overlap: The flood-tablet/Gilgamesh content can brush a history-or-mythology episode; keep the rung on the tablet and its discovery, not the epic's narrative.

name: Egyptian hieroglyphs & the Rosetta Stone
strand: Languages & scripts born in a place
scope: The Nile temples of Karnak and Luxor, the Delta town of Rosetta (Rashid), and the island temple of Philae. T1: on the temple walls along the Nile, HIEROGLYPHS are tiny pictures -- birds, eyes, feet -- that are also SOUNDS, and for ~1,400 years no living person could read them. T2: the key surfaced in July 1799 when a French soldier fortifying Fort Julien near the Delta town of ROSETTA dug up a black slab carrying the same decree three ways. T2: the Rosetta Stone records a priests' decree for young King Ptolemy V (196 BCE) in hieroglyphs (for the gods), Demotic (everyday Egyptian), and GREEK -- and scholars could still read the Greek. T3: the crack in the code was the CARTOUCHE -- the oval loop drawn around a royal NAME -- because a name like 'Ptolemy' had to be spelled out in sound-signs, not pictures. T3: in 1822 Jean-Francois Champollion realized hieroglyphs are BOTH picture-signs and sound-signs mixed together, and reportedly ran to his brother shouting 'I've got it!' before collapsing. T4: Champollion could do it partly because he read COPTIC -- the last living descendant of ancient Egyptian, still chanted in Egyptian churches -- so he knew how the words should sound. T4: the LAST hieroglyph ever carved is dated 394 CE on the temple of PHILAE, an island in the Nile -- after that the knowledge died for fourteen centuries. T4: Britain seized the stone when Napoleon's army surrendered in Egypt (1801) and shipped it to London, where it is the British Museum's most-visited object. T5 (dinner-test): Egyptians wrote hieroglyphs in either direction, and you tell which way to read by which way the animals FACE -- you always read TOWARD their faces. T5: 'hieroglyph' is Greek for 'sacred carving'; the Egyptians called their own script 'medu netjer', the god's words.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosetta_Stone (verified via WebFetch this session: 1799 Bouchard at Rosetta, 196 BCE Ptolemy V, hieroglyphic/Demotic/Greek, Champollion 1822, Young/cartouches), /Egyptian_hieroglyphs, /Jean-Francois_Champollion, /Philae, /Graffito_of_Esmet-Akhom
framing_note: Scene-led, place in every stem (Karnak/Rosetta/Philae/British Museum); invert the wonder -- lead with 'a script no one could read for 1,400 years', make the mechanism the answer (cartouches ring a NAME). Key accuracy rail: hieroglyphs are a MIXED logo-phonetic script, not 'picture-writing' where each symbol is a whole idea -- Champollion's insight was that they carry SOUNDS too. Dinner-test payoff: 'read toward the animals' faces'. Lane border: Napoleon's Egyptian campaign is a history episode -- keep the capture rung on the OBJECT's journey to London, not the war.
history_overlap: The stone's 1801 capture ties to Napoleon's Egyptian campaign (1798-1801), a history-bank episode; keep the rung on the object, not the military campaign.

name: Hangul, the alphabet Korea designed on purpose
strand: Languages & scripts born in a place
scope: Korea under King Sejong the Great (Joseon dynasty); the Hunminjeongeum manuscript. T1: most alphabets grew slowly over centuries, but KOREA'S -- Hangul -- was deliberately INVENTED as a single project, announced by King Sejong the Great in 1443 so ordinary Koreans could finally read and write. T2: Sejong built it to be so easy that (he said) 'a wise man learns it in a morning, a fool in ten days' -- 24 simple letters instead of the thousands of borrowed Chinese characters only nobles had time to master. T3 (dinner-test): the CONSONANT shapes are little diagrams of your MOUTH -- the letter for 'n' pictures the tongue touching the ridge behind the teeth, 'm' is a closed square like sealed lips -- the shape SHOWS you how to make the sound (the only major 'featural' alphabet). T3: the VOWELS are built from three marks -- a dot (heaven), a flat line (earth), and an upright line (a standing person) -- so the alphabet encodes a tiny cosmology. T4: Korea's elite scholars FOUGHT the new script to protect Chinese characters as a badge of learning; the official Choe Manri petitioned the king to scrap it, and Hangul was even banned for stretches. T4: Hangul letters are not strung in a line -- they are stacked into square SYLLABLE BLOCKS, one tidy tile per syllable. T4: the book that introduced it, the Hunminjeongeum ('The Proper Sounds to Instruct the People', 1446), survives as a UNESCO Memory of the World, and UNESCO named its global literacy prize after King Sejong.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangul, /Sejong_the_Great, /Hunminjeongeum, /Choe_Manri, /UNESCO_King_Sejong_Literacy_Prize (standard references; corroborate 1443 creation vs 1446 promulgation at build)
framing_note: Scene-led, place/ruler in the stem (Korea/King Sejong); invert the wonder -- lead with 'an alphabet a fool can learn in ten days', make the DESIGN fact the answer (the letters picture the mouth). Key accuracy rail: Hangul was CREATED 1443 and PROMULGATED 1446 -- if a rung uses a year, use it correctly; and it is a featural ALPHABET, not a syllabary. Dinner-test payoff: consonant shapes are diagrams of the speech organs. No lane conflict; this is a pure cultural-creation-born-in-a-place wonder.

name: Cyrillic & the brothers of Thessaloniki
strand: Languages & scripts born in a place
scope: Thessaloniki (the brothers' home port), Great Moravia, and the First Bulgarian Empire (the Preslav Literary School) where Cyrillic actually formed. T1: more than half a billion people -- Russian, Ukrainian, Bulgarian, Serbian readers -- write in the CYRILLIC alphabet, and the trail leads to two brothers, Cyril and Methodius, from the Greek port of THESSALONIKI. T2: sent north to Great Moravia around 863 to preach in the local Slavic tongue, the brothers first invented a DIFFERENT alphabet -- Glagolitic -- a swirl of loops and crosses built to spell Slavic sounds Greek letters couldn't. T3 (dinner-test / the twist): the alphabet NAMED after Cyril was actually made AFTER he died -- by his DISCIPLES in Bulgaria at the Preslav Literary School (~890s-900s), who kept Greek letter-shapes and borrowed Glagolitic letters for sounds like 'sh' and 'zh'. T3: Cyrillic looks like Greek because it mostly IS Greek uncial letters -- but the extra signs (Zh, Sh, Shch, Yu) were added in Bulgaria for Slavic sounds Greek didn't have. T4: the brothers gave the Slavs their first written language, Old Church Slavonic, which is why Cyril is honored as 'Apostle to the Slavs' and the two share a feast day marked across the Slavic and EU world.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyrillic_script (verified via WebFetch this session: Cyril/Methodius made GLAGOLITIC ~863; Cyrillic built later by disciples at the Preslav Literary School, First Bulgarian Empire, earliest inscriptions ~921), /Saints_Cyril_and_Methodius, /Glagolitic_script
framing_note: Scene-led, place in every stem (Thessaloniki / Great Moravia / Bulgaria). CRITICAL accuracy rail (the whole ladder turns on it): Cyril and Methodius created GLAGOLITIC, not Cyrillic -- Cyrillic was built later by their disciples in BULGARIA and merely named in Cyril's honor. Do NOT write a rung saying 'Cyril invented the Cyrillic alphabet' (the common myth). Dinner-test payoff: the alphabet named after Cyril wasn't made by Cyril. This is settled history, so keep choices as adjacent real facts (Glagolitic vs Cyrillic, Thessaloniki vs Constantinople, Moravia vs Bulgaria) -- no stance needed.

name: Byblos & the Phoenician alphabet that conquered the world
strand: Languages & scripts born in a place
scope: Byblos (Gebal) on the Lebanese coast, its sister ports Tyre and Sidon, and the alphabet's onward road to Greece and Rome. T1: on the coast of Lebanon sits BYBLOS, one of the oldest cities people have never stopped living in -- and the home of the alphabet that, in a way, YOU are reading right now. T2: the Phoenician alphabet did something radical -- it DROPPED the vowels and used just 22 signs for CONSONANTS, small enough that a merchant, not only a priest, could learn to write (an 'abjad'). T2: Phoenicians were the Mediterranean's great SEA-TRADERS, and they carried the easy alphabet on their ships to every port -- it spread by TRADE, not conquest. T3: the oldest long Phoenician text is carved on the stone coffin of King Ahiram of Byblos (~1000 BCE), and it even sets a CURSE on anyone who disturbs the tomb. T3 (dinner-test): our word 'Bible' comes from BYBLOS -- the city was the great port for Egyptian PAPYRUS, so Greeks called the writing-paper 'byblos' and a book 'biblion'. T4: the Greeks borrowed the Phoenician letters around 800 BCE, kept the names and ORDER (aleph->alpha, bet->beta = 'alphabet'), but re-used spare consonant signs as the first true VOWELS -- the missing pieces added back. T4: the letters still hide their old PICTURES -- aleph was an OX-head (flip our 'A' over and you see the horns), bet was a HOUSE, mem was WATER (our wavy 'M'). T5: from Byblos the trail runs Phoenician -> Greek -> Etruscan -> LATIN, so the ABCs of English are great-great-grandchildren of a Lebanese trading script. T5: the same Phoenician root also branched into Aramaic, Hebrew and (through Aramaic) Arabic -- most of the world's alphabets share this ONE Levantine ancestor.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenician_alphabet, /Byblos, /Ahiram_sarcophagus, /Greek_alphabet, /History_of_the_alphabet (standard references; corroborate the 'byblos->Bible' etymology and Ahiram ~1000 BCE dating at build)
framing_note: Scene-led, place in the stem (Byblos / the Lebanese coast; Greece named only as the alphabet's next stop). Invert the wonder -- lead with 'the alphabet you're reading right now', make the concrete fact the answer (it dropped the VOWELS; flip 'A' to see the ox). Key accuracy rail: Phoenician is an ABJAD (consonants only); the Greeks' innovation was adding vowels -- keep that pairing exact. Dinner-test payoff: 'Bible' comes from Byblos. Lane border: this shares the alphabet-origin territory with the Serabit el-Khadim ladder (proto-Sinaitic is the earlier ancestor, Byblos the mature Phoenician stage) -- keep Byblos rungs on the CITY and the Phoenician stage, and let Serabit own the desert-mine birth.

name: Serabit el-Khadim: the alphabet born in a turquoise mine
strand: Languages & scripts born in a place
scope: Serabit el-Khadim, a mountain mining site in the Sinai Peninsula (with its Hathor temple), and the desert road of Wadi el-Hol in Egypt. T1: high in the desert at SERABIT EL-KHADIM in the Sinai, Egyptian crews dug TURQUOISE out of the rock -- and scratched onto those mine walls sits the ancestor of every alphabet on Earth. T2 (dinner-test): the writers were Semitic-speaking WORKERS, not scholars or kings -- they grabbed a few Egyptian hieroglyphs and used each picture for its FIRST SOUND (a house-picture, 'bayt', became the sound 'b'), inventing the first alphabet around 1800 BCE. T3: in 1916 Alan Gardiner cracked a word that repeats in these scratches -- l-b-'-l-t, 'to BAALAT (the Lady)', the goddess of the mine -- confirming that desert miners, not a royal court, took the first step toward the ABCs.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proto-Sinaitic_script (verified via WebFetch this session: Serabit el-Khadim + Wadi el-Hol, ~1900-1800 BCE, Petrie 1904-05 discovery, Gardiner 1916 reading 'to Baalat' via acrophony from hieroglyphs), /Serabit_el-Khadim
framing_note: Scene-led, place in the stem (the Sinai turquoise mine). Invert the wonder -- lead with 'the ancestor of every alphabet', make the surprise the answer (invented by MINERS, not kings). Key accuracy rail: proto-Sinaitic derives from Egyptian hieroglyphs by ACROPHONY (picture -> its first sound); date it ~1900-1800 BCE and flag that the exact century is debated (early vs late dating). Dinner-test payoff: the alphabet was invented by desert workers. This is the early-birth gem that feeds the Byblos/Phoenician ladder -- keep it on the Sinai origin, not the later Phoenician spread.

name: Norse runes & the Jelling stones
strand: Languages & scripts born in a place
scope: Jelling in Denmark (the two royal runestones), the Rok stone in Sweden, and Viking-age Scandinavia. T1: Vikings didn't write with pens -- they CARVED runes, an alphabet of straight strokes (no curves) made to be cut into WOOD and STONE with a knife. T2: the runic alphabet is called the FUTHARK, after its first six letters -- just as 'alphabet' comes from alpha and beta. T2: at JELLING in Denmark stand two royal stones; the large one, raised by King Harald 'Bluetooth' around 965 CE, brags that he 'won all Denmark and made the Danes Christian' -- Denmark's 'baptismal certificate', its birth record in stone. T3: that Jelling great stone carries the oldest picture of CHRIST in Scandinavia -- shown tangled in branches like a warrior on a tree, a freeze-frame of the moment the Norse gods gave way to Christianity. T4 (dinner-test): the BLUETOOTH symbol on your phone is King Harald Bluetooth's initials -- the runes Hagall and Bjarkan merged into one bind-rune -- because the tech 'unites' devices as Harald united Denmark. T4: in Sweden the ROK runestone (~800 CE) is the longest runic inscription -- over 700 runes of riddles and a lost heroic tale, carved across all five faces of the slab. T5: runes are angular ON PURPOSE -- curves are hard to slice across wood grain or stone, so every stroke is a clean straight cut, and runes had no fixed reading direction.

KEY accuracy rail: the Bluetooth NAME from Harald Bluetooth is documented, but the exact 'logo = his bind-rune' story is a popular claim, not in the primary Jelling record -- frame that rung as 'the popular story goes...', don't state the bind-rune as settled fact. Also keep runes as an ALPHABET for carving, not a magic system. Dinner-test payoff: the Bluetooth symbol. Lane border: Harald's unification/Christianization of Denmark is a history episode -- keep the rung on the STONE and what it says, not his reign's politics.

name: Sequoyah & the Cherokee syllabary
strand: Languages & scripts born in a place
scope: The Cherokee homeland of the southern Appalachians (Tennessee, Georgia, the Carolinas), and the Cherokee Nation carried west to Oklahoma. T1: in the Cherokee country of the southern Appalachian mountains, a man named SEQUOYAH did something no other person in recorded history is known to have done alone -- he built a complete writing system from scratch, and he could not read a single word of ANY language. T2: his system is a SYLLABARY, not an alphabet -- about 85 symbols, one for each Cherokee SYLLABLE (like 'ga', 'no', 'hi') -- so a Cherokee speaker could learn to read in days, not years. T3: his neighbors first feared it as witchcraft, so he proved it by having his young daughter Ayoka read out messages he could not have overheard -- and within a few years much of the Cherokee Nation was LITERATE. T3: by 1828 the Cherokee were printing their own newspaper, the Cherokee Phoenix, in both Cherokee and English -- the first Native American newspaper. T4: Sequoyah borrowed the SHAPES of some letters from an English spelling book because he liked how they looked, but gave them completely different sounds -- so a Cherokee 'R' or 'D' sounds nothing like ours. T4 (dinner-test): the giant SEQUOIA and the towering redwoods (Sequoiadendron) are widely said to be named for him -- a man who gave his people writing lending his name to the biggest trees on Earth. T5: the syllabary is still alive -- on Cherokee Nation road signs, phone keyboards, and even a Cherokee-language message NASA carried to space -- and it survived the nation's forced removal west, the Trail of Tears.

Dinner-test payoff: the giant sequoias carry his name. Lane border: the Trail of Tears (1838 removal) is a major history-bank episode -- name it once as the backdrop the script survived, but do NOT make a rung about the removal itself.

name: The Inca quipu: an empire written in knots
strand: Languages & scripts born in a place
scope: The Inca Empire run from Cusco across the Andes (Peru). T1: the Inca governed a mountain empire of millions from CUSCO in the Andes -- with roads, storehouses and a census -- yet had NO written words; they recorded everything in KNOTTED STRINGS called quipu (khipu). T2: a quipu is a counting machine -- knots tied at different HEIGHTS on a hanging cord mean ones, tens, hundreds -- a base-10 place-value system you read with your FINGERS. T3 (dinner-test): the KIND of knot carries the digit -- a figure-eight knot means one, a long knot's turns count two through nine, and a bare GAP with no knot means ZERO -- the Inca kept a place for zero. T3: special officials called KHIPUKAMAYUQ ('knot-keepers') created and memorized the records -- tribute, llama herds, storehouse grain -- and could be punished with death for an error. T4: we can read the NUMBERS on a quipu, but the COLORS and cord-patterns may hide names or words we still can't read -- a knotted 'language' that could be part story, still undeciphered. T5: Spanish priests BURNED thousands of quipu as 'idols of the devil', so only about 1,400 survive today -- the Inca's own records largely destroyed by the men who conquered them.

name: Linear B & the burnt tablets of Knossos
strand: Languages & scripts born in a place
scope: The palace of Knossos on Crete, the Mycenaean mainland, and the 1952 decipherment. T1: in the ruins of the palace of KNOSSOS on the island of CRETE, diggers pulled up thousands of clay tablets covered in a script no one could read -- labelled 'Linear B'. T2 (dinner-test): the tablets survived by ACCIDENT -- they were soft, sun-dried scrap records meant to be wiped and reused, but the palaces BURNED down, and the fire baked them into permanent bricks. T2: Sir Arthur Evans, who excavated Knossos from 1900, found TWO scripts and named them Linear A (older, Minoan) and Linear B (younger) -- and guarded his tablets so jealously he barely let rivals see them. T3: for fifty years Linear B beat everyone; Evans was CERTAIN it wasn't Greek -- the Minoans, he insisted, were their own separate people. T4: in 1952 Michael VENTRIS -- an ARCHITECT, an amateur, not a professor -- cracked it, and the answer stunned scholars: Linear B was an early form of GREEK, proof the Mycenaeans from the mainland had taken over Crete. T4: the tablets turned out to be INVENTORIES, not poems -- lists of sheep, chariot wheels, swords and jars of honey, plus offerings to gods whose names (Zeus, Poseidon, Athena) already appear 3,000+ years ago. T5: Ventris built a codebreaker's GRID of sign-patterns to crack it -- then died in a car crash at 34, weeks before his great book appeared. T5 (the door still shut): Linear B's PARENT, Linear A -- the Minoans' own language -- is STILL undeciphered; we can sound out the signs but don't know the language, so the Minoans stay silent.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linear_B, /Knossos, /Arthur_Evans, /Michael_Ventris, /Linear_A (standard references; corroborate Ventris 1952 decipherment and the 'baked by palace fire' preservation at build)
framing_note: Scene-led, place in the stem (Knossos / Crete). Invert the wonder -- lead with the mystery/surprise, make the fact the answer (an AMATEUR architect cracked it; the answer was GREEK). Key accuracy rail: Linear B = Mycenaean GREEK (Ventris/Chadwick 1952); Linear A (Minoan) remains UNDECIPHERED -- keep the two straight, and note the tablets were administrative lists, not literature. Dinner-test payoff: the records only survived because the palace burned. Lane border: Minoan/Mycenaean civilization is history territory -- anchor every rung on the SCRIPT and the PLACE (the tablets, Knossos), not the Bronze Age political story.
history_overlap: Minoan/Mycenaean civilization overlaps history-bank content; keep rungs on the script and Knossos-as-place, not the Bronze Age geopolitics.

name: The Indus script & the silent seals of Mohenjo-daro
strand: Languages & scripts born in a place
scope: Mohenjo-daro and Harappa, the great cities of the Indus Valley Civilization (in today's Pakistan). T1: 4,500 years ago the Indus city of MOHENJO-DARO (in today's Pakistan) had brick streets on a grid and covered drains -- and a WRITING that not one person on Earth can read today. T2: the Indus script survives mostly on tiny stamp SEALS -- carved stones about the size of a coin, many showing a one-horned 'UNICORN' bull standing above a short line of signs. T2: the inscriptions are maddeningly SHORT -- usually only about five signs, never a long passage -- so codebreakers have no 'paragraph' to get a grip on. T3: there are roughly 400+ different signs -- too many to be a simple alphabet, too few to be one-picture-per-word -- so scholars can't even agree WHAT KIND of script it is. T4 (dinner-test / the wall): the deepest problem is that we don't know the LANGUAGE the Indus people spoke, and there is no Rosetta Stone for it -- so unlike Egyptian or Linear B, the Indus script may NEVER be read. T4: the little seals traveled far -- Indus seals turn up in Mesopotamian cities like Ur, proof of a sea-trade network -- yet even those foreign clues can't unlock the signs.

Invert the wonder -- lead with 'a script no one can read', make the reason the answer (the inscriptions are only ~5 signs; the LANGUAGE is unknown). name: Rongorongo, the lost script of Easter Island
strand: Languages & scripts born in a place
scope: Rapa Nui (Easter Island), the loneliest inhabited island on Earth. T1: EASTER ISLAND (Rapa Nui), the most isolated inhabited island on the planet, holds a second riddle besides its stone giants -- RONGORONGO, rows of tiny carved glyphs on wooden tablets, the only writing ever invented anywhere in the Pacific. T2 (dinner-test / the strange rule): you read rongorongo in 'reverse BOUSTROPHEDON' -- start at the bottom-left corner, read a line, then FLIP the whole tablet 180 degrees to read the next line, which was carved upside down. T3 (the tragedy): almost every tablet was lost -- burned or scattered, and after the 1860s Peruvian slave raids and the missionaries the last people who could read it were gone; only about two dozen objects survive, and NO ONE can read them today.
source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rongorongo, /Easter_Island (standard references; corroborate reverse-boustrophedon reading, ~26 surviving objects, undeciphered status, and the 1860s slave-raid collapse at build)
framing_note: Scene-led, place in the stem (Rapa Nui / Easter Island).
